title: Speculative Kernel Prober and Prefill Warmup to Reduce FlashAttention v3 Cold-start Regressions
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Since rolling out FlashAttention v3 we have intermittent cold-start latency and occasional workspace allocation failures for uncommon sequence-length shapes. Symptoms manifest as large first-request TK latency spikes and sporadic OOMs in prefill when a new worker encounters an unseen (batch_size, seq_len) shape. Root causes include deferred kernel workspace probing, on-demand kernel selection that triggers heavy compilation or allocation, and lack of a safe lightweight warmup path for v3 kernels.

Proposal: Implement a speculative kernel prober + prefill warmup subsystem that runs at worker startup and opportunistically on first few model shapes. Goals are to: (1) detect the cheapest compatible kernel variant for observed shapes (v3/v2/compat), (2) pre-allocate minimal safe workspace for the fastest variant, and (3) execute a micro-prefill (<=8 tokens per stream) to populate KV caches and kernel autotuner state. The prober must be low-overhead, opt-outtable per-customer and per-tier, and avoid synchronous blocking of live requests (use background warmup or short-circuit to fallback kernels).
acceptance_criteria: median first-token prefill latency reduction >= 25% for previously unseen shapes compared to baseline
95th percentile first-request latency spikes reduced to within 2x steady-state latency for >= 95% of observed shapes
no increase in steady-state tail latency or sustained throughput regressions after enabling prober
prober can be disabled via customer config and defaults to off for Free/Trial accounts
automated e2e test coverage and canary rollout plan documented
steps_taken: Collected perf traces from canary cluster (canary-rt-7) showing 3x spikes on first prefill for shapes (b=4, s=4096) and (b=1, s=8192)
Reproduced regression in local perf harness using model: redwood-gpt-7b-quant and flashattn-v3 with workspace fallback to v2

Prototype implemented: background prober thread that attempts lightweight kernel-run with a single stream of 4 tokens; records run-time and workspace requirement; stores result in per-worker shape cache
Benchmarks: prototype decreased median cold-start prefill latency from 420ms -> 290ms for shape (4,4096) on A100-40GB; tail spike occurrences reduced from 7% -> 1.2% across sampled runs
Security review: initial design reviewed with infra-security; no secret handling required but we added RBAC toggle for enterprise disablement
decision_log: 2026-03-11: Chose speculative background probe over synchronous probing to avoid blocking request thread (agreed by eng leads)
2026-03-11: Use micro-prefill of <=8 tokens to warm KV cache instead of full prefill to limit cost and side effects
2026-03-12: Cache results keyed by (model_id, batch_size, seq_len_bucket) rather than exact seq_len to bound cache size
2026-03-12: Default prober disabled for low-tier customers; enable-by-default for dedicated/reserved capacity customers
comments: Marco Liang (2026-03-11): Prototype shows promise but we need stronger canary metrics and a rollback plan if warmup triggers memory pressure.
Priya Nair (Perf): Please add histogram of workspace allocations and confirm no sustained increase in GPU resident memory after warmup.
Erik Johansson (QA): Add determinism checks for micro-prefill to avoid observable output differences for deterministic models. If micro-prefill mutates RNG state we should seed consistently.
Design note (2026-03-12): UX for customer controls - add toggle in Console under 'Advanced runtime settings' + API flag in create_model_route
next_steps: Finish safety checks: enforce max speculative workspace per GPU (configurable), add OOM guard and eviction path
Add e2e canary plan: 1% of Hosted production traffic -> 5% -> 25% with automated rollback triggers on tail latency or memory pressure
Expand probe shapes: sample real traffic histogram to create seq_len buckets and pick top 12 shapes for prewarm
Implement Admin API and Console switch to opt-out per-customer and a per-route opt-in flag
Write unit tests for prober cache eviction and deterministic micro-prefill behavior
